entities.name: Zhuansun Shi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zhuansun Shi, commonly known by his courtesy name Zizhang, was a prominent disciple of Confucius who accompanied him in his travels abroad and later started his own sect of Confucianism. Born into a noble family in the state of Lu during the Eastern Zhou period, Zhuansun Shi spent most of his life in the service of the various rulers of the region.


 As a key figure associated with the development of Neo-Confucian thought, Zhuansun Shi's teachings emphasized the importance of moral values and personal cultivation. His philosophical ideas had a significant impact on the intellectual landscape of ancient China, influencing the work of later Confucian scholars such as Han Feizi.


 Despite his influential role in shaping the course of Chinese philosophy, Zhuansun Shi remains relatively unknown to modern readers outside of academic circles. However, his contributions to the development of Neo-Confucian thought continue to be studied and debated by scholars today.
